narrative.overview: Every screen is signed by its place before it shows a number. The system borrows four things from the enamel street plaques of Brazilian cities and nothing else: their blue, their condensed capitals, their density, and the plate itself. Navigation, controls and layout are the standard ones of a working web application.
keyCharacteristics: A place plate heads every screen, from city down to a street block and its number range.
Wayfinding yellow has one meaning: you are here.
Each city zone owns a strip colour, used only to identify the place.
Every number is tabular; every figure carries its provenance.
Asking prices and sale prices are tagged and never share a style.

rules.name: The One Job Rule
rules.body: Yellow means you are here. It is never a warning, a highlight, a badge or a decoration.

rules.name: The Zone Rule
rules.body: A zone colour identifies a place. It never encodes a value, a state or a trend.

rules.name: The Neutral Movement Rule
rules.body: Movement is orange and blue and always carries a sign or a word; green and red are reserved for state.

rules.name: The Two Prices Rule
rules.body: An asking price carries the outlined Asking tag; a recorded sale price carries the solid green Sale tag.

rules.name: The Capitals Rule
rules.body: Uppercase is for place names on a plate and for tags.

rules.name: The Flat Rule
rules.body: A shadow means this sits over something else.

dos: Do open every screen with a place plate.
Do put a provenance line under every figure.
Do tag every price as Asking or Sale.
Do label model-written text as written by a model.
donts: Don't build a grid of listing cards with a photograph and a price.
Don't render questions and answers as chat bubbles.
Don't arrange figures as a row of KPI cards.
Don't use yellow for anything except you are here.
